WorkSync 0.3.0 adds Releases: the software a project delivers, as a
timeline, with Excel import and export.

## Download

| System                    | File                              |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Windows (64-bit)          | `WorkSync-win32-x64-0.3.0.zip`    |
| macOS (Apple silicon)     | `WorkSync-darwin-arm64-0.3.0.zip` |
| Linux (no install)        | `WorkSync-linux-x64-0.3.0.zip`    |
| Linux, Debian or Ubuntu   | `worksync_0.3.0_amd64.deb`        |
| Linux, Fedora or openSUSE | `worksync-0.3.0-1.x86_64.rpm`     |

- **Windows:** unzip into a folder on a local drive and run `worksync.exe`.
  Nothing is installed. To update, unzip the new version in the same place as
  the old one: your data is in the `WorkSync-data` folder next to it and stays.
- **macOS:** unzip and move `WorkSync.app` to Applications.
- **Linux:** unzip and run `worksync`, or install the package.

The builds aren't code signed yet, so Windows and macOS warn the first time.
See [Download and run](https://github.com/KelvinNguyen97/WorkSync#download-and-run)
for how to open the app anyway. Your data from 0.2.0 is kept and upgraded; a
backup is made first.

## New

- **Releases.** Turn it on for a project in Choose views. It opens on a
  timeline: one milestone per release day, with its files. Click a file to see
  what changed, why and how it was checked, and the version it replaced; "No
  info" where nothing is written.
- **Each file has its own** change log, purpose and verification (the
  release's text is shown when a file has none), and you can add your own
  file fields, such as a ticket number.
- **Versions and Modules tabs:** the version of every module on each server or
  platform at each release date, and the latest version of each file.
- **Import from Excel:** one row per released file, headings in English or
  Japanese. A preview shows what is added, updated or skipped and which rows
  have problems, before anything is saved. Rows that repeat the same file
  (from sheets put together) become one file. "Copy instructions for AI"
  helps convert a customer's sheet, and WorkSync's own export imports back.
- **Export:** Excel, an HTML page, or both.
  - Excel in the usual layout: the module version list, the latest
    versions and a change log per product, oldest first.
  - Or your own template: save the default template, change it in Excel, and
    choose it. The template goes along when the project is exported.
  - The HTML page is one file that opens offline in any browser, with the
    timeline, a product filter, Expand all, and printing on white.

Please report problems on the
[Issues page](https://github.com/KelvinNguyen97/WorkSync/issues).
